the_bottleneck_named_last_round: the validator set is the ceiling

already_in_the_project: a_refusal_is_a_specification_v1: a refusal NAMES A KIND -- 601 on the enlarged openssl census yielding certificate, key, parameters, shared library, crl
a program's verdict on a file IS a judgement about that kind: gzip -t rejects what is not gzip, unzip -t what is not zip
round 10 excluded `cat` for accepting everything, which is the property a fake judge has
the_observation.conclusion: a judge does not need to be typed; it needs to be MEASURED against a probe pair

admission_conditions: DISCRIMINATION: exit 0 on a real file of the kind and non-zero on a decoy
DETERMINISM: the same file judged twice gives the same verdict
NO SIDE EFFECTS: the tree must be unchanged after judging
the_loop.probe_source: the real member of every pair is written by the library or archiver that defines the kind (zipfile, gzip, json.dump, tar -cf, the interpreter), never typed by me
the_loop.authority: the probe pair, not the candidate table

refused.why: python -c 'gzip.open(p,"rb")' is LAZY: it reads nothing and returns a handle for any file, exit 0 on real AND 0 on decoy -- this is `cat`

measured.the_ceiling_moves: bz2 and xz: unreadable () under the typed set, readable ('bz2',)/( 'xz',) after one earn call each, with zero new validator code and no change to the four other files
measured.bad_guesses_refused: lazy bz2.open -> 0/0 refused; bzip2 -d (decompresses, wrong direction) -> 0/2 refused; cat -> 1/0 refused

defects_found_by_measuring.why: that is perfectly valid UTF-8, so utf8_text accepted it and was reported as `cat`. The refusal was CORRECT and my probe was wrong: a decoy one kind accepts turns that kind's judge into a false positive
defects_found_by_measuring.fix: decoy is 0xFF bytes, which cannot begin a UTF-8 sequence and is not any other kind

defects_found_by_measuring.defect: python and utf8_text were absent from CANDIDATES
defects_found_by_measuring.why: I assumed they were not earnable; measured, both separate the pair cleanly. The omission was mine, not a limit of the loop

a_defect_in_round_10_found_while_auditin.defect: census() collapsed two different statements into UNKNOWN
a_defect_in_round_10_found_while_auditin.evidence: all 13 files round 10 called UNKNOWN in intake/ were accepted by utf8_text -- they were unknown only because memory had never recorded that exact SUBSET of validators, which is memory's bookkeeping, not the file's problem
a_defect_in_round_10_found_while_auditin.harm: it aimed the next round's learning at markdown the machine could already read, and inflated the unknown count
a_defect_in_round_10_found_while_auditin.fix: three verdicts: KNOWN (signature recorded), UNDERSTOOD (a declared validator reads it, subset is new), UNREAD (nothing accepts it). Only UNREAD is queued for learning
a_defect_in_round_10_found_while_auditin.measured_after: intake/: 27 KNOWN, 13 UNDERSTOOD, 0 UNREAD, learn queue empty (correctly)

honest_limits: a candidate argv is still supplied by me; the loop decides WHETHER it is a judge, not which program to try. Choosing the program automatically is the next step and is NOT done
the probe pair needs a producer for the kind, so a kind with neither a producer nor a library on this machine cannot be earned here
seven is still small; the point is that adding the eighth is one probe pair rather than new code
the scan uses earned judges through earned_validators() but still falls back to the typed table when a program is absent
no benchmark task was run; this is a mechanism measurement
authority NONE, sandbox only, independent verification OPEN
next_bottleneck: choosing WHICH program to try as a judge, without me naming it: the environment declares its own judges the same way it declared its own producers in round 9, and the probe pair decides whether the declaration was honest
